"According to received information, some groups and individuals have entered the rather part of Mostar towards west Herzegovina who will try to include an extreme individual -- extreme individuals from the municipality, Citluk and Ljubuski, to their formations. With this they will attempt to interrupt bringing of fresh manpower to Mostar town. "In the past period of war, we did not have any problems with Muslim people or single persons in the area of said three municipalities. Even they were frightened in the past time because they remained minority. Especially after the clashes in Jablanica and Konjac, when plenty BiH Army members were brought to the Ljubuski prison. By brigade command, I suggested disarmament of the Muslim soldiers through total returning of soldiers after coming from the frontline."

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I stood up before the question was put to the witness on purpose. I really think that we should have a basis established before the question is put. I can see what has been read, the question hasn't been put, so there's not a leading question, but we should ask the witness what he knows about Ljubuski and what he knows about this period. A minute ago, the witness said he knew what happened in June. This document is from May. I think a basis should be established to see whether a witness knowing anything about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel, allow your colleague to do her work. That's as important as your work. And she will respond to the objections when putting questions. When the Defence rises, I always have the impression that they think that the Prosecution is going to make mistakes. Well, let's wait to see how the things unfold. We don't know anything about this in advance.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. Buljan, do you remember on direct testimony talking about the municipality of Ljubuski? Do you remember those questions being asked?

utterances.speaker: STIPO BULJAN
utterances.text: I remember having confirmed something in regard of a document. I said that at the time those same people performed those duties and that such a document could be signed. As far as Ljubuski itself is concerned, well, perhaps I had once passed through Ljubuski, or perhaps never.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: This document is dated May 7th of 1993, and understanding that you were not -- you were still in the Posavina at the time but nonetheless you were aware, as you've testified, that there were the differences between the Croats and Muslims relations, there was a difference between that relationship and the similar relationship, the Posavina, had you heard about these aggravated relations between the BiH -- excuse me, between the Muslim and Croat HVO members and Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: STIPO BULJAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Sir, can you go to 4901632.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you held a position in the army, or there's a minor paragraph that I'm extremely interested in. It's the last paragraph in the document, where the person who drafted the document who is in charge of the SIS says the following, it's his point of view: "I think," he says, "that is it is time to take energetic measures, and that concerns the Ministry of Interior in particular, because we are in a war zone and it is difficult for an army to take preventive or repressive measures." So the person who drafted this document has situated the problem very well. He says that the problem with the Muslims, but in his opinion it's for the Ministry of Interior to concern itself with this problem, it's not for the army to do that. So what do you think about this?

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Counsel, Your Honours, I apologise. There is a mistake in the English translation. In the Croatian it says "because we are not in a war zone." That's what it says in the original document. And the contrary is stated, it says "because we are not in a war zone," and I think that this has given rise to confusion. In the original it says "not."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Then we will rephrase this. On the 7th of May, the person who drafted the document said that he believed that they were not in a war zone, but nevertheless he says that it is for the Ministry of Defence to take certain measures against these Muslims. It's not for the army to intervene or to take repressive or preventive measures against them. So what is your opinion of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm not familiar with this document. It's the first time I've seen it. I have never seen it before. As far as Ljubuski is concerned, I've never analysed that town. The Prosecutor has repeated on two or three times something. I'm not sure I have the same document in front of me. Are you talking about the document drafted in Ljubuski on the 7th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave I would like to clarify something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that you are not familiar with this document. The 103rd Brigade, it's not in Ljubuski, fine, that's not the issue. What I would like to know, because I'm approaching this from a different point of view, but at the level of your brigade could someone have drafted the same kind of document and stated that it was for the Ministry of Interior to concern itself with such an issue? That is what I'm interested in, sir. To say, well, he is not familiar with the document and so on and so forth, well, that's irrelevant. I'm dealing with this from another angle. So could someone in your brigade have drafted such a document, such a statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could someone have written this and sent it to someone without the commander being aware of the fact; is that what you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I'll abandon that question. It seems too complex to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel, Your Honours, I think it would be useful if we could clarify something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Madam Alaburic, we are approaching 7.00. In view of our discussion yesterday evening, I dearly feel that it is not a very proper way, to say the least, that in the last half an hour or one hour the Prosecutor was not allowed to -- really to proceed according to her friends. And I request all of you to be really -- in a way accept those problems which are, of course, connected to all of the witnesses appearances here, but let her continue her work, and then, of course, you will be free to do whatever you wish, you would like to, and to ask any other questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to add something. The person who will have liberty to act will just be the person who has additional questions in respect to Ms. Nozica's questions. I've given up the question so don't go back to the issue, Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours, I just wanted to draw your attention to the following: I think that your question is of exceptional importance and it would be good to establish why this SIS official --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, because as a rule when I ask questions it's very important, but if the witness doesn't understand my question then I will abandon the question. I won't insist on putting the question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, Your Honours, in the two paragraphs earlier reference is made to what the police has to establish, so your question is quite abstract. If we can't see that the SIS official has doubts according to which some members of ABiH from the Bregova [phoen] Brigade are hiding in villages in the territory of the municipality of Ljubuski, and he believes that, therefore, the civilian police should involve itself in the affair because Ljubuski is not in a war zone. So I think we are now familiar with all the facts and it might be easier for all the witness to comment on this subject given that he doesn't know the document, he is isn't familiar with the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It is now almost 7.00, so we will adjourn now. The Prosecution has an hour and a half at its disposal tomorrow. I would like to invite the Defence, as Judge Prandler rightly said, I invite the Defence to allow the Prosecution to do its work. The Prosecution is doing its work. We don't know what the Prosecution wants to demonstrate so allow them to proceed -- those questions that were different from the questions posed by the Prosecution. So we will meet tomorrow at 2.15. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 12th day of February 2009, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.58 p.m.
